This strathspey is generally called Miss Lyall or Miss Lyall’s in Shetland, Scotland, and Cape Breton.

The Cat That Kittled In Jamie’s Wig

I have recently seen these lines in a collection of Perthshire Ballads, Rhymes and Fragments:

Anti-Jacobite Fragments

The cat has kittled in Charlie’s wig,
The cat has kittled in Charlie’s wig,
There’s ane o‘ them living, and twa o’ them dead,
The cat has kittled in Charlie’s wig.

Miss Lyall, X:4

Transcription of the tune as it appears in Gow’s Repository of the Dance Music of Scotland, part 4 (1817), where it is called Panmure House. Gow notes that the Strathspey is “very old” but does not give a composer.
